    - text: Matrix shows integers 1..12 and at most the first ten selected primes.
    - complementary:
      - heading "Inspect Factorization" [level=3]
      - text: Integer n
      - spinbutton "Integer to factor": "12"
      - strong: 12 = 2^2 × 3
      - paragraph: This integer is represented in the expansion of the selected finite prime product.
      - text: A finite prime product includes infinitely many integers made only from those primes. It is not the same truncation as the first N integers.
      - button "6"
      - button "18"
      - button "30"
      - button "42"
      - button "84"
      - button "210"
    - img
    - text: These series and product representations converge to the same value for real s > 1. At s = 1, both diverge.
    - article:
      - heading "Convergence Boundary" [level=2]
      - paragraph: The positive-term series converges for real s > 1.
      - paragraph: The ordinary prime product also converges there.
      - button "Explain analytic continuation"
    - article:
      - heading "Analytic Continuation" [level=2]
      - paragraph: ζ extends meromorphically with a simple pole at s = 1.
      - math: ζ ( 0 ) = − 1 2 , ζ ( − 1 ) = − 1 12
      - paragraph: ζ(−2n) = 0 for positive integers n.
    - article:
      - 'heading "Practice: Understand ζ(2)" [level=2]'
      - paragraph: Relate the series, primes and increasing approximations.
      - button "Start Practice":
        - text: Start Practice
        - img

    - group "Complex plane mode":

    - img "Listed zero pairs on real part one half": "-40 -20 0 20 40 -1 0 0.5 1 2 Re(s) Im(s)"
    - paragraph: "Critical line: Re(s) = 1/2."
    - article:
      - heading "First Non-Trivial Zeros (Approx.)" [level=2]
      - button "s ≈ 1/2 ± 14.134725142i"
      - button "s ≈ 1/2 ± 21.022039639i"
      - button "s ≈ 1/2 ± 25.010857580i"
      - button "s ≈ 1/2 ± 30.424876126i"
      - button "s ≈ 1/2 ± 32.935061588i"
      - button "More zeros":
        - text: More zeros
        - img
      - text: Listed heights reuse the repository’s sourced zero table; the plot is not a proof about all zeros.
    - article:
      - heading "Riemann Hypothesis" [level=2]
      - paragraph: The conjecture states that all nontrivial zeros lie on Re(s) = 1/2.
      - paragraph: Showing finitely many zeros cannot prove this statement.
      - 'link "Learn more: NIST zero reference"':
